units.name: Unit PaHub v2.0

power.logic_voltage_status: do not derive GPIO logic voltage from the 5V supply label

protocol.summary: PCA9548A 6-channel I2C mux at 0x70 (A0-A2 straps select 0x70-0x77). A single-byte channel bitmask is read-modify-written: select sets bit(channel), release clears it; all passthrough I2C operations wrap select->transfer->release.
gaps: PCA9548A is an 8-channel part; the unit page/driver expose only 6 channels (CHN0..CHN5).
A0-A2 solder-pad address straps are not modeled.
Downstream bus forwarding / nested hubs need multi-bus runtime support that does not exist yet.
0x70 conflicts with env-iii (QMP6988 0x70); 0x71-0x77 are free.

claims: passthrough wrappers select/release around every I2C call

runtime.required_data_plane: SoC I2C transactions to a device-local PCA9548A-compatible mux at 0x70: 1-byte channel mask read-modify-write; downstream forwarding/nesting is NOT modeled in the draft

units.blocker: 0x70 conflicts with env-iii; the PCA9548A is 8-channel while the unit page/driver expose 6; nested/multi-address passthrough needs a runtime multi-bus extension that does not exist yet.
limitations: All defaults are synthetic fixtures, not measured hardware values.
Downstream slave traffic, nested hubs and A0-A2 straps are NOT modeled in the draft.
Bus capacitance, polling latency, hot-plug and electrical behavior are NOT RUN.
0x70 conflicts with env-iii (one Unit per bus).

units.name: Unit PbHUB v1.1

power.logic_voltage_status: do not derive GPIO logic voltage from the 5V supply label

protocol.summary: I2C 6-channel PORT.B expander at 0x61. Each channel has base address [0x40,0x50,0x60,0x70,0x80,0xA0]; a single command register is channel_base|offset. Digital IO0/IO1 = 0x00/0x01 write, 0x04/0x05 read; PWM = 0x02/0x03 write, 0x02/0x03 read mapped 0-255<->0-100; analog read 0x46 (2B LE); RGB count 0x48 (2B LE), single LED 0x49 (2B LE pos + 3B GRB), range 0x4A (2B LE begin + 2B LE count + 3B GRB), brightness 0x4B (1B 0-100), servo 0x42/0x43; 0xFE fw, 0xFF address; 0xFA RGB mode.

registers.encoding: RGB count / single LED / range / brightness

gaps: Firmware v1 vs v2: v2 adds SK6812 support and I2C IAP; the v2 protocol/IAP commands are not modeled.
The product page Protocol table is an image/PDF; the driver is the line-by-line source here.
MCU identity remains conflicted across the product page (STM32F030F4P6), the I2C address index and the old U041 page (MEGA328).
0x61 conflicts with pbhub (U041); channel bases conflict with encoder/scroll (0x40), nfc/acssr (0x50), dac (0x60), env-iii (0x70).

rgb-frames.label: 每通道最后 RGB 帧

claims: firmware v1/v2 (v2 adds SK6812 and IAP)

runtime.required_data_plane: SoC I2C transactions to a single 0x61 command space with channel_base|offset register bytes (reuse 0131 CONTROL_PBHUB); downstream channel ports are not separate I2C addresses

units.blocker: Same protocol family as the implemented pbhub (U041) and reuses 0131 CONTROL_PBHUB, but v1/v2 firmware (SK6812/IAP) is not modeled; 0x61 conflicts with pbhub and the channel bases conflict with encoder/scroll/nfc/acssr/dac/env-iii.
limitations: All defaults are synthetic fixtures, not measured hardware values.
Firmware v2 SK6812/IAP commands are NOT modeled; the page Protocol table is not line-by-line parsed.
MCU identity (STM32F030F4P6 vs MEGA328/I2C index) remains unresolved.
Servo/RGB electrical behavior, nested hubs and channel electrical levels are NOT RUN.
0x61 conflicts with pbhub; one Unit per bus.

units.name: Unit RGB LED 10cm / 15LED

power.logic_voltage_status: do not derive GPIO logic voltage from the 5V supply label

protocol.summary: SK6812 single-wire RMT LED strip (A035 = 15 LEDs). unit/rgb.py RGBUnit(port,number) instantiates driver/neopixel SK6812 on port[1] (PORT.B yellow). Frames are 24-bit GRB per LED at 800kHz; the neopixel driver ORDER=(1,0,2,3) stores G,R,B in the buffer and bitstreams the whole buffer in one write.
gaps: LED optics/power/timing tolerance and color perception are NOT RUN.
A035 variants (15/29/72/144/288 LEDs) differ only by count; each needs its own confirmed count.
SK6812 GRB byte order and brightness scaling are driver-SHA sensitive.
The product page's strip-side wire colors (VCC/GND/DATA) are not the Grove controller mapping; use the PORT.B PinMap for controller wiring.

claims: SK6812 subclass of NeoPixel with br scaling

runtime.required_data_plane: SoC RMT bitstream capture on PORT.B yellow (unit/rgb.py passes port[1]); guest writes 24-bit GRB frames per LED

units.blocker: RMT capture can reuse the implemented fader/rgb path, but LED optics/power/timing and variant counts are unresolved; driver SHA sensitive.
limitations: All defaults are synthetic fixtures, not measured hardware values.
LED optics/color/power and RMT timing tolerance are NOT RUN.
SK6812 GRB order and brightness scaling depend on the pinned neopixel driver SHA.
Other A035 variants need distinct LED counts; electrical behavior is not modeled.

units.name: Unit OP90

power.logic_voltage_status: do not derive GPIO logic voltage from the 5V supply label

protocol.summary: 90-degree non-contact photoelectric limit switch: an object blocking the IR beam drives the white Digital Output. The driver reads Pin(port[0]=white, IN, PULL_UP) active-low and optionally counts both edges via IRQ (COUNTER mode).
gaps: Optical alignment/IR beam/object size/speed and 90-degree geometry are NOT RUN.
Active-low polarity is the driver default; the page only labels Digital Output.
PORT.B is required; atoms3r/sticks3/stopwatch have no PORT.B.

units.blocker: GPIO digital input can reuse the implemented limit/pir path, but optics/90-degree beam behavior are NOT RUN and PORT.B is required.
limitations: All defaults are synthetic fixtures, not measured hardware values.
IR optics/beam alignment/object speed and 90-degree geometry are NOT RUN.
Active-low polarity comes from the driver default; the page has no explicit polarity table.

units.name: Unit LoRaE220-433

power.logic_voltage_status: do not derive GPIO logic voltage from the 5V supply label

protocol.summary: UART LoRa module: config commands 0xC0 (write, 11-byte frame [0xC0,0x00,0x08,addrH,addrL,REG2,REG3,REG4,REG5,cryptH,cryptL]) and 0xC1 (read, [0xC1,0x00,0x08], 8 extra bytes); transparent/P2P send frame target_address(2B BE)+target_channel(1B)+payload; receive may append an RSSI byte. Driver uses 9600 8N1 while the product page says 115200.

registers.encoding: write config: addr, REG2 baud/parity/airrate, REG3 subpacket/noise/power, REG4 channel, REG5 rssi/mode/lbt/wor, crypt

gaps: Product page UART 115200 vs driver 9600 is a real conflict (unresolved).
DIP M0/M1 mode switch (config/transparent/WOR) is not modeled by the driver.
RF/antenna/433MHz range/air rate and power are NOT RUN.
0xC0/0xC1 firmware/response-length assumptions and RSSI-byte handling are unresolved.
UART host must have PORT.C; shares UART with other UART units (one per UART).

claims: P2P send target 2B BE + channel + payload

runtime.required_data_plane: SoC UART transactions on PORT.C (yellow=unit RX, white=unit TX) with a device-local 0xC0/0xC1/P2P frame responder; RF link NOT modeled

units.blocker: Page UART 115200 vs driver 9600 conflict; DIP mode switch/RF/antenna/433MHz physics are unresolved; UART host must be PORT.C and share no UART with another Unit.
limitations: All defaults are synthetic fixtures, not measured hardware values.
RF/LoRa/antenna/range/air rate/power and DIP M0/M1 modes are NOT RUN.
Baud rate 9600 (driver) vs 115200 (page) is unresolved; pin one source at implementation time.
Config response length/RSSI-byte/encryption semantics are not fully modeled.
PORT.C-only hosts; one UART per Unit.
